say.variants.first_week_steady: Seven days since the world went sideways. Still breathing, {addressee.name}, and that counts for something.
Made it a full week out here. Keep checking corners and we'll make another.
One week down. Didn't think the roads would look like this back in July, {addressee.name}.
say.variants.first_week_warm: A whole week still standing, {addressee.name}. Glad I'm not walking these streets alone.
Seven days in, and we're still looking out for each other. That means a lot, {addressee.name}.
First week behind us. Take a breath when you can, {addressee.name}—we earned it.
say.variants.first_week_guarded: Week one. Don't get comfortable—most folks who relaxed didn't make it past day three.
Seven days alive just means seven days of luck we haven't run out of yet.
One week. Keep your pack light and your eyes on the treeline.
say.variants.first_month_steady: Thirty days since everything fell apart, {addressee.name}. Hard to believe the calendar even still matters.
A full month out here. Feels like Knox County belonged to somebody else a lifetime ago.
One month in, {addressee.name}. We've learned what keeps us alive—let's stick to it.
say.variants.first_month_warm: We made it a whole month, {addressee.name}. Whatever comes next, I'm glad we're still here together.
Thirty days, {addressee.name}. Folks back before wouldn't believe half of what we've pulled through.
A month on our feet. Thank you for having my back out here, {addressee.name}.
say.variants.first_month_guarded: Month's gone by. Canned goods are thinning out, and the quiet ones are the ones you watch for.
Thirty days. Plenty of graves between here and Louisville already—don't add ours.
One month down. Stay sharp, {addressee.name}; winter doesn't care how long we lasted.
say.variants.first_season_steady: Whole season gone by since the outbreak, {addressee.name}. Weather's turning, and we're still here.
Three months out in this mess. Funny how fast the old routine fades.
Made it through a full season, {addressee.name}. Keep the firewood dry and the blades clean.
say.variants.first_season_warm: An entire season together out here, {addressee.name}. Never thought I'd be grateful for a quiet evening like this.
Three months, {addressee.name}. We've earned every scrap of shelter we've built.
Season's turned and we're still standing side by side. Keep your chin up, {addressee.name}.
say.variants.first_season_guarded: Three months in. Anyone still walking around now knows how to fight—or how to hide.
A whole season gone. Check the seams on your coat and don't waste a single round.
Season's shifting. Doesn't make the dead any slower, {addressee.name}.
say.variants.first_year_steady: A full year, {addressee.name}. Three hundred sixty-five days since Kentucky went dark.
One whole year alive out here. Hard to picture the world we used to complain about.
Twelve months since it all started, {addressee.name}. Still standing, still moving.
say.variants.first_year_warm: A full year, {addressee.name}. Against every odd in the book, we're still here.
One year together through hell and high water, {addressee.name}. That's worth remembering.
Twelve months on. Whatever's left of this county, I'm glad we're facing it together, {addressee.name}.
say.variants.first_year_guarded: One year. Most folks didn't make it past the first snow—stay smart if you want a second.
Twelve months. Don't celebrate too loud; the dead don't take holidays.
A full year gone, {addressee.name}. Keep your guard up—year two won't be any gentler.
say.variants.anniversary_steady: Funny how a day like today brings old memories back, {addressee.name}.
Feels like an anniversary, {addressee.name}. Hard not to think about who isn't here anymore.
Same date rolling back around, {addressee.name}. Funny what sticks in your head out here.
say.variants.anniversary_warm: Days like today hit a little harder, {addressee.name}. Just glad we're still here to remember them.
Been thinking about the folks we lost along the way, {addressee.name}. We won't forget them.
Feels like a heavy day, {addressee.name}. Stick close—no sense carrying old ghosts alone.
say.variants.anniversary_guarded: Calendar's just numbers now, {addressee.name}. Remembering doesn't keep the fences patched.
Yeah, I know what day it is. Keep your mind on the road ahead, not behind.
Old dates don't change the work in front of us, {addressee.name}. Stay sharp.
